A [[Dathomirian/Legends|Dathomirian]] [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] [[Gender/Legends|male]] was the '''father''' of the eventual [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Darth Maul/Legends|Darth Maul]]. They were a member of the [[Nightbrothers/Legends|Nightbrothers]], a group of [[Soldier/Legends|warriors]] who operated on<ref name="Darth P" /> the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomir]] and were subservient to the [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsisters]] [[Coven/Legends|coven]] of the [[Witches of Dathomir]]. After Maul's [[Parent/Legends|mother]],<ref name="Darth P" /> [[Talzin/Legends|Talzin]]<ref name="Son of Dathomir Three">[[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 3|''Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir'' 3]]</ref> gave [[Reproduction/Legends|birth]] to Maul<ref name="Darth P" /> in [[54 BBY/Legends|54 BBY]],<ref name="Death" /> and in keeping with tradition which required the death of a Nightbrother after their child's birth, Maul's father was [[Death/Legends|killed]] within a [[Standard year/Legends|year]] of Maul's birth.<ref name="Darth P" /> After Maul was [[Thief/Legends|stolen]] by Talzin's associate, the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]], and became his [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]],<ref name="Son of Dathomir Three" /> he considered the possibility that his parents had spent [[Time/Legends|time]] searching for him<ref name="EpIJournal">''[[Star Wars Journal: Darth Maul]]''</ref> and did not know that his father had died.<ref name="Darth P" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Where is the infant's father?''"<br />"''Dead&mdash;by tradition.|Darth Sidious and Kycina, who was previously established to be Maul's mother|<ref name="Darth P" />}}
Maul's father was first mentioned, albeit indirectly, in the [[2000]] novel [[Star Wars Journal: Darth Maul|''Star Wars Episode I Journal: Darth Maul'']], written by [[Jude Watson]]. While the father of Maul himself is not mentioned, the book contains references to Maul's parents.<ref name="EpIJournal" /> Maul's father was first directly mentioned in the [[2012]] novel [[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']], written by [[James Luceno]].<ref name="Darth P" />

Several sources, including ''Darth Plagueis'', suggest that Maul's mother is the [[Witch/Legends|witch]] [[Kycina]].<ref name="Darth P" /> However, the [[Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir 3|third issue]] of the [[Star Wars: Darth Maul — Son of Dathomir|''Star Wars: Darth Maul—Son of Dathomir'']] [[Star Wars comic books|comic]] series, written by [[Jeremy Barlow]]<ref name="Son of Dathomir Three" /> and released on [[July 16]], [[2014]],<ref name="Dark Horse SoD3">{{DarkHorse|url=Comics/24-767/Star-Wars-Darth-Maul-Son-of-Dathomir-3|text=Star Wars: Darth Maul&mdash;Son of Dathomir #3}}</ref> establishes Talzin as Maul's mother instead.<ref name="Son of Dathomir Three" /> As ''Son of Dathomir'' is the more recent source, this article assumes it takes precedence. In ''Darth Plagueis'', upon having been asked by Darth Sidious as to the presence of Maul's father, Kycina responds that the father is dead by tradition.<ref name="Darth P" /> While Kycina herself was retconned, the information regarding Maul's father may still hold true, as it does not conflict with what ''Son of Dathomir'' establishes.
